svg.text: Saab 99 LE, model 1974 — Ignition and starting
118e GN/VT 1.0 ← ignition switch 20:15, via 58 ign. switch (power sheet)
On the car an aftermarket rev counter is wired in series at this end of the ballast resistor, between the
resistor and its green-and-white feed (check D1). Not drawn yet: which of the green-and-white leads here
go through it is still open.
95f VT 1.0 → reversing lights, via 60 inhibitor reversing (signals sheet)
84e GL 1.5 ← ignition switch 20:50, via 58 ign. switch (power sheet)
probably on to 59 cold start: start signal
The distributor’s contact breaker points switch the coil’s terminal 1 to earth. The injection’s
trigger contacts are in the distributor too (injection sheet).
Ballast resistor 6 lowers the coil’s voltage while the engine runs. While cranking, starter
terminal 16 feeds the coil’s side of it directly (119e SV 1.0), so the coil gets full voltage for
Switch 90 is drawn in P: start contact closed, reversing contact open (it closes in R).
Seat-belt warning contact 88 on the gear selector: probably not fitted
(it goes with a belt warning lamp).
Relay 89 and switch 90 let the starter turn only in P or N: with the ignition on, switch 90’s start
contact (closed in P and N) energises relay 89, which joins 84a GL 1.5 to 84b GL 1.5 and so
Relay 89 is drawn as the factory wired the 1974 automatic. This car is a 1973 chassis, so
whether it has relay 89 is check F1. A car without the relay has a short jumper (84c GL 1.5)
across the two pins of 57 starter line; a 1973 automatic may run the starter line through switch 90
A cable is labelled with its colour and size (7 BR/VT 1.0),
a part with its name (7 Distributor).
Thin black lines without a label: leads with no cable number.
